Old parish registers can be a real puzzle to parse, but this ledger is beautifully detailed once you get a feel for the handwriting.

This appears to be a Catholic marriage register from Ireland, spanning late **1863** on the left page and early **1864** on the right page. Each entry typically lists the **date**, the **bride and groom**, and their **witnesses** (often denoted by a small "W" or "Wit"). You will also notice a few Latin entries regarding "dispensation" for couples who were related by blood (consanguinity).

Parish: **North Tipperary** (Diocese of Killaloe, Borrisoleigh / Cloughjordan / Templederry area). **NOT our family's parish** — our Gleeson line is in Hospital parish (Cashel & Emly diocese, ~50 mi south, on the Limerick/Tipperary border). Saved here for reference in case future records link the North Tipperary Gleeson cluster to our line; not indexed in MEMORY.md (name-only matches in a different diocese).

Gleeson entries of note:
- **Oct 12, 1863** — Wm Carroll m. Honora Gleeson
- **Jan 29, 1864** — James Gleeson m. Honora Gleeson; witnesses John Gleeson + Cath Gleeson (same-surname marriage — either unrelated families or a kin marriage with dispensation on an adjacent page)
- **Feb 6, 1864** — Daniel Gleeson m. Anne Maher

> **A Quick Tip on the Places Mentioned:** The mentions of **Borrisoleigh**, **Cloughjordan**, and **Templederry** firmly place this register in **County Tipperary, Ireland**. If you are building out a family tree, knowing these specific townlands/parishes will be incredibly useful for hunting down later civil records!
